sections.hypothesis: Among liquid coins, those where takers bought the largest share of the past week's volume beat the average coin over the next week in spot, beyond their own past week and size, by more than a weekly round trip.
sections.rationale: Who pays: aggressive (taker) buying is demand that crosses the spread to get filled now, often informed or flow-driven; if it is slow to be absorbed, it predicts further buying pressure, paid for by liquidity providers and late sellers. Kestrel's 5-minute order-flow test failed on costs; at a weekly horizon costs are a small share of a move. Outside evidence, unverified: the outside AI review cited a 2026 paper finding that crypto order flow predicts returns after controlling for past returns, more strongly weekly than daily; not read here, a lead only. The control for the past week's return is the point: aggressive buying rises with price, so without it this would be momentum by another name (Kestrel's weekly momentum on ETH failed its holdout). Data: the taker-buy quote volume Binance publishes in every daily bar, already stored.
sections.rules: kestrel cross-study taker-flow --research <this note>. Signal: the sum of taker-buy quote volume over the 7 days to the Sunday close, over the sum of quote volume. Universe: the exploration half of research/exploration/split.toml plus BTC, ETH and SOL (the locked confirmation half is never read). Daily bars before 2025-11-01. Each Sunday close (the bar opening Sunday 00:00 UTC), a coin is eligible with 180+ days of history and a 30-day median daily quote volume of 20M USDT or more. Next week: log return from that close to the close 7 days later (a missing bar leaves that coin-week out). Controls: the past week's log return and log of the 30-day median volume. Each week with 10+ eligible coins carrying the signal: next-week returns regressed on the z-scored signal, past week and size; the signal's coefficient averaged over weeks (Fama-MacBeth), P(mean > 0) by 5,000 bootstrap resamples of weeks (seed 0). Long-only: each week the top fifth of coins by signal against the average eligible coin.
sections.falsification: PROCEED to a strategy note only if the signal's mean coefficient is positive with P(> 0) of at least 90%, AND the top fifth beats the average eligible coin by more than one weekly round trip: 2 x (7.5 bps fee + 8 bps half-spread, the 20M-100M band) = 0.31% a week. Otherwise KILL. Run once. The overlap with the past week's return is reported whatever the verdict.
sections.parameters: 7-day flow window, Sunday closes, the eligibility rule above, fifths, 5,000 resamples: fixed before the run. No other window or cut is tried.
sections.costs: As the funding study: one round trip a week is the hurdle. A study, not a strategy run: one look, logged in the findings.
